verdicts.reason: Moving the cast inside the shift on line 56 can change how wide the shift is evaluated. Depending on the tool's sizing rules, the top bits of base_clks<<strike_level can be lost at HICCUP_BASE_W, which gives a smaller cool_down_target and changes when line 96 matches and hiccup_done rises.
Without line 85, the asynchronous reset no longer clears hiccup_done. At power-up it stays X, and a reset that arrives while it is 1 leaves it at 1, which shows on the output port.
Line 99 assigns cool_counter to itself inside an always_ff. Removing it leaves cool_counter unassigned on that path, so the flop keeps its value anyway and nothing changes.

Line 99 only runs in the same branch where line 98 sets hiccup_done to 1, so the first match happens at the same time as before. After that, hiccup_done can only be cleared by reset or !hiccup_active (lines 85 and 91), and both also clear cool_counter (lines 84 and 92). cool_counter is not a port, so the different value it holds until then is never seen, and hiccup_done is the only output.

Line 99 only runs as hiccup_done is set to 1 on line 98, and hiccup_done stays 1 until reset or !hiccup_active, which also clear cool_counter (lines 84 and 92). Setting the internal counter to all-ones in between, or letting it wrap from there, never changes hiccup_done, the only output.

The inverted counter on line 99 is written only once hiccup_done has been set to 1 (line 98). hiccup_done cannot drop until reset or !hiccup_active (lines 82-92), and those branches also set cool_counter to 0, so the changed counter never reaches the output.
